title: African Leadership Academy: admission to the Class of 2027 (two-year diploma)
overview: A two-year residential pre-university diploma programme near Johannesburg for young leaders from across Africa and the world; admitted students can receive need-based financial assistance.
program_dates: Admitted students arrive on campus in August 2027 (ALA 2027 application guide)
deadline_text: Early Decision deadline "October 15, 2026"; Regular Decision deadline "January 15, 2027". Early Decision results in January 2027, Regular Decision results in April 2027 (ALA apply page and 2027 application guide, read 12 October 2026).
funding_details: ALA: tuition is USD 30,900 per year and "African Leadership Academy fees are all-inclusive, including tuition, accommodation, meals, and uniforms."

ALA: "97% of ALA students receive financial assistance"; admitted applicants are "eligible to receive significant financial assistance in the form of scholarships", decided after admission according to family financial means.
The 2027 application guide says all finalists can apply for financial aid.
participation_fee: USD 30,900 a year (all-inclusive), reduced by need-based financial aid for most students
age_requirement: "For admission in 2027, applicants must have been born on or after September 1, 2007."
experience_requirement: No work experience; essays ask about a time you identified a need in your community and took action
nationality_requirements: Admits students from across Africa and around the world; ALA states it does not discriminate on the basis of nationality
language_requirement: Applications accepted in English, French and Portuguese
documents_required: A piece of work completed in the past year and a half (not a certificate or transcript)
Letters of recommendation and financial aid documents at the finalist stage
application_process: Register and apply online on the ALA apply page
Finalists are interviewed and can apply for financial aid
potential_issues: Full fees are USD 30,900 a year; how much aid a student receives is decided only after admission
Very selective: ALA reports a 4% acceptance rate
The apply page labels the 15 July 2026 opening as "for the class of 2026" while the deadlines are for the Class of 2027
The page does not say whether there is an application fee
action: Read the ALA apply page and application guide, then apply online before 15 January 2027 (Early Decision closes 15 October 2026).

title: AU Theme of the Year 2027: logo and visual identity competition for young African creatives
organization: African Union Commission (Infrastructure and Energy Department), with AUDA-NEPAD
overview: An online design competition for individual young Africans aged 18 to 24 to create the official logo and visual identity of the African Union's Theme of the Year 2027, with cash prizes for the top three entries.
program_dates: Call open 24 September to 23 October 2026; the winning logo is unveiled at the AU Summit
deadline_text: "Submission deadline / Friday, 23 October 2026 at 23:59 East Africa Time (UTC+3)" (AU terms of reference, read 12 October 2026). The au.int event page shows the call ending "Oct 23, 2026 - 15:00".
funding_details: AU: "USD 5,000 First place", "USD 2,000 Second place", "USD 1,000 Third place", plus a certificate, recognition on AU platforms and training opportunities.
AU: "The winner will also have the opportunity to participate in the AU Summit"; travel arrangements are not described.
experience_requirement: "Students, designers, artists, digital creatives, innovators welcome — formal qualifications not required"
nationality_requirements: Citizens of all African Union member states
language_requirement: Unknown / Not specified (terms of reference published in English and French)
eligibility: Citizen of an AU member state
Individual entries only, one entry per person
Original, human-made work: generative AI is not permitted
AU personnel, contractors, evaluators and their immediate family are not eligible
documents_required: Presentation PDF with the primary logo, colour, black-and-white and reversed versions and three mock-ups
Preview PNG/JPEG at least 3000 px wide
Concept note of up to 500 words
Signed originality, intellectual-property and AI declaration
application_process: Download the terms of reference and declaration form from the AU competition page
Submit the package through the official competition entry form reached from that page
Shortlisted applicants must send editable vector files within 3 working days
potential_issues: The winner assigns copyright and IP rights in the design to the AU Commission
Generative AI tools are banned and entries are checked
The event page shows 15:00 on 23 October while the terms of reference say 23:59 EAT: submit early
The entry form link was not found on the page as read; use the link the AU page provides
action: Read the AU terms of reference and submit your logo package through the AU entry form before 23 October 2026.

title: SafeTech Africa HackLab 2026: youth social innovation challenge
organization: UNFPA (East and Southern Africa and West and Central Africa regions) with the Spotlight Initiative, the African Union and other UN partners
overview: A youth innovation challenge for young Africans aged 18 to 35 with digital or community solutions against technology-facilitated violence, child marriage and FGM; finalists get virtual mentorship and pitch at the YouthConnekt Africa Summit.
program_dates: Applications 29 September to 18 October 2026; virtual showcase for shortlisted teams; final pitch at the YouthConnekt Africa Summit in November 2026
deadline_text: "Closing Date: 18 October 2026 (23:59 CAT)" (Spotlight Initiative call page, read 12 October 2026).
funding_details: Call: "Four winners will receive seed grants ranging between USD 5,000 to USD 10,000."
Shortlisted finalists receive pitch coaching and present live at the YouthConnekt Africa Summit; travel for the pitch is not described.
experience_requirement: An original, practical innovative idea or solution; no prior experience is stated
nationality_requirements: Young African innovators; the residency criterion links to the UNFPA East and Southern Africa list of countries, while the call names both the East and Southern and the West and Central Africa regions
language_requirement: Unknown / Not specified (call published in English)
eligibility: Young African innovators, social entrepreneurs or digital rights advocates, individually or in teams
Solution under one of three themes: safe physical and community spaces, safe information spaces, safe digital spaces
application_process: Read the call on the Spotlight Initiative page
Submit through the online form linked from that page before 18 October 2026

sources.label: Spotlight Initiative: SafeTech Africa HackLab call

potential_issues: Whether DRC residents qualify is not clear: the residency rule links only to the UNFPA East and Southern Africa country list
Applications go through a Google Form linked from the official page
action: Read the call on the Spotlight Initiative page, check the residency rule for your country, and apply through the linked form before 23:59 CAT on 18 October 2026.

title: Yoma (Youth Agency Marketplace): free online courses, tasks and opportunities
organization: Yoma, developed by UNICEF with partners and young Africans
overview: A free digital platform where young people take self-paced online courses and impact tasks, earn verified digital credentials and tokens, and find jobs and other opportunities from partner organisations.
duration: Self-paced; each opportunity lists its own effort (for example 1 to 15 hours)
deadline_text: No deadline: registration is open and most learning opportunities are listed as "Ongoing" (yoma.world, read 12 October 2026). Some individual opportunities have their own end dates.
funding_details: Yoma: "Boost Your Employability - 100% for free" and "Yoma is completely free".
Yoma: learners can "earn digital tokens that can be cashed out or redeemed in the Yoma marketplace", for example airtime, data and grocery vouchers.
stipend: None (digital tokens can be earned on some opportunities)
age_requirement: Unknown / Not specified (aimed at young people)
experience_requirement: No experience needed for learning opportunities
nationality_requirements: No nationality condition stated: "No matter who you are or where you're from, Yoma is built to open doors for every young person."
language_requirement: Yoma says the platform "is available in five languages"; the languages are not listed on the pages read
eligibility: Young people anywhere; create a free account (YoID)
application_process: Choose opportunities (courses, tasks, events, jobs) and complete them to earn verified credentials
potential_issues: Many listed jobs and some courses are only for Nigeria or South Africa; filter by country
Courses are offered by third-party partners whose quality varies
Not a job or internship by itself
action: Create a free account on yoma.world and filter opportunities by your country and language to find courses you can take now.
